original_value: Individuals with mobility impairments related to age, injury, or disease, often require the help of an assistive device (AD) such as a cane to ambulate, increase safety, and improve overall stability. Instrumenting these devices has been proposed as a non-invasive way to proactively monitor an individual’s reliance on the AD while also obtaining information about behaviors and changes in gait. A critical first step in the analysis of these data, however, is the accurate processing and segmentation of the sensor data to extract relevant gait information. In this paper, we present a highly accurate multi-sensor-based gait segmentation algorithm that is robust to a variety of walking conditions using an AD. A matched filtering approach based on loading information is used in conjunction with an angular rate reversal and peak detection technique, to identify important gait events. The algorithm is tested over a variety of terrains using a hybrid sensorized cane, capable of measuring loading, mobility, and stability information. The reliability and accuracy of the proposed multi-sensor matched filter (MSMF) algorithm is compared with variations of the commonly employed gyroscope peak detection (GPD) algorithm. Results of an experiment with a group of 30 healthy participants walking over various terrains demonstrated the ability of the proposed segmentation algorithm to reliably and accurately segment gait events.

result.paraphrase: Individuals with age-, injury-, or disease-related mobility impairments often rely on an assistive device (AD) such as a cane to walk, enhance safety, and improve overall stability. Instrumenting these devices has been proposed as a non-invasive means of proactively tracking a person’s dependence on the AD while also gathering information about behavior and gait changes. A crucial first step in analyzing such data is accurate sensor-data processing and segmentation to extract relevant gait information. In this paper, we introduce a highly accurate multi-sensor gait segmentation algorithm that is robust across a range of walking conditions with an AD. It combines a loading-information-based matched filtering approach with angular-rate reversal and peak-detection techniques to identify key gait events. The algorithm is evaluated across multiple terrains using a hybrid sensorized cane capable of measuring loading, mobility, and stability information. The reliability and accuracy of the proposed multi-sensor matched filter (MSMF) algorithm are compared with variants of the commonly used gyroscope peak detection (GPD) algorithm. An experiment with 30 healthy participants walking on various terrains showed that the proposed segmentation algorithm can reliably and accurately segment gait events.
